speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: I must clarify that Pyelonephritis (a kidney infection) does not typically present with a large ovarian mass or significant abdominal girth; those findings suggest a gynecological or hepatic issue. Can you tell me if you have noticed any changes in your menstrual cycles, or if you experience pain in your lower abdomen or pelvis? REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic_Ultrasound: Findings: A palpable mass on the right side of the pelvis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That ultrasound confirms a pelvic mass on your right side. Given the combination of a large ovarian mass, shortness of breath, and increased abdominal girth, have you been experiencing any nausea, vomiting, or a feeling of fullness soon after eating? Also, do you have a history of cancer in you or your immediate family?

REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis
REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis: Large heterogeneous mass in the right ovary with significant ascites; right-sided pleural effusion; no obvious metastatic lymphadenopathy; liver parenchyma appears normal.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Cancer (likely epithelial origin). The combination of a large heterogeneous ovarian mass, ascites, and a right-sided pleural effusion (likely a pseudomyxoma peritonei or malignant ascites tracking upward) is classic for advanced ovarian malignancy. The absence of liver metastases and lymphadenopathy supports a primary ovarian origin. I recommend immediate surgical consultation for staging and potential cytoreductive surgery.
